answer: Picture it as a grove that lanterns through the network, tracked on a shared onyx: an agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive in time rather than money: every alias must post a bond that unlocks only after a graded work period, so a fresh clone starts at zero and must survive scrutiny to climb. A herd of fake identities cannot share one bond, each pays the full waiting cost, and the total cost grows faster than the number of fakes because each must independently earn its reputation. The attacker pays in elapsed time, which cannot be bought or parallelized, while honest age...
